steps.text: Place vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper into a blender. Turn the blender on; pour in olive oil in a slow, steady stream. Blend until salad dressing is smooth and emulsified, 10 to 15 seconds.

raw_recipe.headline: Maple-Balsamic Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: This balsamic and maple vinaigrette dressing with Dijon mustard is delicious on chicken or shrimp salads. Also doubles as a marinade for pork!
raw_recipe.name: Maple-Balsamic Vinaigrette

recipeInstructions.text: Place vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper into a blender. Turn the blender on; pour in olive oil in a slow, steady stream. Blend until salad dressing is smooth and emulsified, 10 to 15 seconds.

review.reviewBody: This is awesome - we used this on our salad (baby mixed greens and arugula) the past two nights (with pear slices the first night and avocado the second), and my husband is still raving about it! Having read the reviews first, I used equal parts of balsamic and maple syrup, and a little bit less olive oil(proportionately), but kept the mustard (dijon, because that's what we like best), pepper, and a pinch of the salt. I used my mini-food processer to blend everything together, and it has stayed emulsified (yet not thickened, like mayo); don't know if the processer is what did the trick, but the dressing sticks to the greens, rather than sinking to the bottom of the bowl. Thanks for a great recipe! This will be wonderful with winter salads (sugared nuts, goat cheese) ... yum!

I did it a bit differently, made this way from Canadian Maple it is way too sweet, to get the sweet and sour effect try white vinegar and less maple and no mustard, that way you don't mask the maple flavor and the sweetness is balanced out.
125 ml white vinegar 70 ml canadian maple syrup (dark amber, grade A), 1 teaspoon salt, dash of black pepper and 250 ml extra virgin olive oil. Add syrup, salt and pepper to vinegar and whisk well till combined and salt is dissolved, gradually add oil while whisking till combined. Use on leafy and seafood salads.

This is good! After reading some of the quantity comments, I used only 1/3 cup of apple cider vinegar and also reduced the olive oil to 3/4 cup. I added 3 T orange juice which really brought out more flavor in comparison. I made a gallon for a fund-raising event and had several requests for the recipe. It was tossed with broccoli florets, toasted sunflower seeds, finely chopped carrots, chopped bacon, and dried cherries.

I was looking for a dressing similar to the one used in Chick fil a's Kale Salad. This recipe is better! I've made it a few times. The 1st time it was a little to vinegary for me. I now double the maple syrup and mustard. Delish! I make a mean kale salad and let the dressing marinate on the greens for about an hour. I used a good quality olive oil and vinaigrette; and real maple syrup.
Delicious! 4 stars because I prefer a sweeter dressing, so I reduced the balsamic vinegar to 1/4 c and the olive oil down to 3/4 c; I left everything else the same.

Wow! This one's really good! I used real maple syrup and canola oil instead of olive oil. I just whisked it in a bowl and then shook it up in a jar to finish emulsifying. We won't hesitate to make this one again!!

I followed the recipe and then adjusted and added a bit more Dijon. I omitted the salt but did use black pepper. I added crumbled bacon to the dressing. I made a spinach salad with toasted almonds, cranberries and sunflower seeds. I used large pink, grilled shrimp with a touch of garlic on top of the spinach salad and it was great! Thanks for the awesome vinegrette!

This was great! I think it tastes like an expensive restaurant's dressing. It would be great with a goat cheese, walnut, cranberries and mixed green salad. I didn't take out the blender, I just whisked it to combine. I also added a tablespoon or so of mayo to give it gloss.
So very good. I have also made it replacing the maple syrup with honey and adding two cloves of garlic. So versatile, simple, and so much better than anything store bought.

I’d use this dressing sparingly, it’s flavor is powerful but delicious and super easy to make! I made sure to use high quality ingredients such as pure maple syrup, not the standard stuff. This is a great dressing!

The oil/vinegar ratio was off for my tastes too much oil and I only used 3/4 cup of oil. I also felt like it was too sweet. I added another teaspoon of mustard and a tablespoon of mayo whisked in to help it stay blended for longer and to tone down the sweetness. That help a lot. I served it with a salad of butter lettuce, goat cheese, dried cranberries and spicy roasted pecans
I love this recipe. I used 3/4 cup maple balsamic instead of adding the balsamic vinegar and maple syrup separately and folloed the exactly for the other ingredients. Delicious!
Delicious! I made this dressing for the roasted butternut squash salad and it was a hit! Followed the recipe to a T!
Wonderful dressing. Made for a Fall salad which had fresh greens, thinly sliced pears, halved grapes, toasted pecans and feta. Received multiple compliments on the salad, especially the dressing.
I little sweet, but really like it
Love this recipe. We use it as a dip for boneless sweet Thai chili wings
Top shelf recipe. Followed it exactly and it's fantastic!
